Connection settings

With "auto" the launcher opens the game port on your router (UPnP or NAT-PMP) so guests can connect directly. If that is not possible, guests connect through the relay automatically. If you forwarded the port yourself, enter your public IP address; for players in your own home network you can enter this PC's LAN address instead.

    Native could not start, so Classic (0.95.0) is used for now.

    Copy your co-op heroes to the Native engine? Your Classic heroes stay as they are. You are asked only once.

    Native (DLL) plays your own Azeroth Survivors with the new co-op engine. Classic (0.95.0) is the previous co-op and always there as a fallback. Everyone in a room needs the same engine and game version; each engine keeps its own heroes.

    Native needs a copy of your own game in the co-op folder (your game install is only read, never changed).

    Your heroes

    Saves

    Co-op saves: …

    Co-op heroes file:

    First start: the co-op begins with new heroes. To play with your single-player heroes instead, press "Import my single-player heroes".

    Separate: the co-op has its own heroes and never touches your single-player save. Shared: the co-op plays with your single-player heroes and writes its progress back (not recommended).

      Share saves with single-player?

      Shared saves link the co-op with your single-player save. The co-op runs game 0.95.0; mixing its save with a newer single-player game can lose heroes, talents or unlocked zones. The co-op keeps backups and merges only what changed in the co-op, but nothing is risk-free. Your single-player save is backed up automatically before the switch. You can switch back to separate saves at any time.

      Choose your own class and gear. Everyone joins the host’s map. Any player can pause or resume the party.

      Four heroes. One adventure.

      How to begin your adventure
      1. Enter your name, then create a room or join a party.
      2. Invite your friends. The host starts when the party is assembled.
      3. The game opens in its own window. Choose your class and gear there.

      Talent choices and chest purchases belong to each character. Guests should follow the launcher’s map-entry indicator before entering the world.
